head: He forgot his wallet.
Or so the story goes.
slides.sub: How Diners Club won two kinds of customers at once.

image.label: A restaurant table in 1940s New York with the bill waiting
image.brief: 1940년대 뉴욕 고급 식당의 테이블. 다 먹은 접시 옆에 계산서가 놓여 있고, 남자 실루엣이 빈 양복 안주머니를 더듬는 장면. 따뜻한 텅스텐 조명, 필름 누아르 톤. 로고 없음.

head: A dinner, a bill,
and no cash.
body: A story often told: in 1949, New York businessman Frank McNamara finished dinner and found he had left his wallet at home. The embarrassment, the story says, gave him an idea.
Years later, an early partner reportedly said the tale was mostly a publicity story.

image.label: A waiter holding a check beside a worried diner
image.brief: 턱시도 차림 웨이터가 계산서를 들고 서 있고, 식사한 남자 실루엣이 난처해하는 모습. 1940년대 맨해튼 식당 분위기. 실존 인물 얼굴 묘사 금지.

head: Credit existed.
It just didn't travel.
body: Department stores and oil companies already gave loyal customers charge cards. But each card worked at one company only.
A salesman entertaining clients across town still needed a wallet full of cash, and a different account at every place he ate.

image.label: A wallet stuffed with single-store charge plates and cash
image.brief: 1940년대 지갑 속에 여러 상점 전용 금속 차지 플레이트와 지폐가 뒤섞여 있는 클로즈업. 실제 상표 디자인 없음.

head: One card for many places.
Two customers to win.
body: In 1950, McNamara and Ralph Schneider launched Diners Club: one card, accepted at many restaurants, with the bill paid in full each month.
But restaurants wanted diners before signing up. Diners wanted restaurants before carrying the card.

image.label: A restaurant owner and a diner facing each other across a doorway
image.brief: 식당 문간을 사이에 두고 마주 선 식당 주인과 손님 실루엣. 서로 상대가 먼저 움직이길 기다리는 구도. 1950년 뉴욕 거리.

head: Nobody joins first.
How do you start?
body: You have an idea and very little else. Both sides are waiting for the other.

options.text: Make restaurants pay a cut of each bill, and seed a small, busy circle of restaurants and diners
options.feedback: This asks restaurants to give up margin on every meal. It only works if the diners really show up. Keep swiping.

options.text: Charge cardholders a big fee and let restaurants join for free
options.feedback: Restaurants would sign up easily, but few people would pay a lot for a card with nowhere to use it. Keep swiping.

options.text: Wait until you can sign hundreds of restaurants across the country
options.feedback: A big network is more convincing, but it could take years and a lot of cash before anyone carries the card. Keep swiping.

image.label: A blank cardboard card on a desk next to a phone
image.brief: 1950년 사무실 책상 위 아무것도 인쇄되지 않은 판지 카드, 다이얼 전화기, 메모지. 결정의 긴장감이 느껴지는 조명.

slides.label: roughly what restaurants paid Diners Club on each bill, as widely reported
body: Cardholders paid only a small yearly fee. Restaurants paid most of the cost. In return, Diners Club paid them and took on the job, and the risk, of collecting from diners.

image.label: A restaurant ledger with a small percentage marked off each bill
image.brief: 식당 장부에 계산서마다 작은 비율이 떼어져 표시된 장면. 1950년대 펜글씨 장부, 따뜻한 종이 질감.

head: Start small.
Start where people eat.
body: The founders began with a small group of Manhattan restaurants and handed cards to a few hundred friends and business contacts, many of them people who ate out on expense accounts.
For a restaurant, the card meant customers who came back and spent freely.

image.label: Businessmen at a busy Manhattan lunch counter in 1950
image.brief: 1950년 맨해튼의 붐비는 식당에서 정장 차림 남자들이 점심을 먹는 장면. 얼굴은 흐릿하게 처리. 활기찬 분위기.

head: From restaurants
to the whole trip.
body: As more diners carried the card, more restaurants joined, and more people wanted it. Hotels and other travel businesses followed, and the club spread beyond New York and abroad.
By 1958, American Express and Bank of America had launched cards of their own.

image.label: A 1950s traveler at a hotel desk handing over a card
image.brief: 1950년대 호텔 프런트에서 여행객 실루엣이 카드를 건네는 장면. 여행 가방, 회전문, 따뜻한 조명. 실제 카드 디자인 없음.

head: Two sides, one network.
Pick who pays.
body: A card is only useful if both diners and merchants use it. Diners Club broke the deadlock by starting in one dense spot, where a few hundred people ate at the same places.
Then it charged the side that gained most per sale, the restaurants, and kept the card cheap for the people who had to carry it.

image.label: Lines connecting diners and restaurants on a city map
image.brief: 뉴욕 지도 위 손님 점과 식당 점이 선으로 이어지며 점점 촘촘해지는 네트워크 그래픽.

head: If two sides need each other,
start small and dense.
body: A network grows from one place where both sides already meet, priced so the hesitant side joins easily.
**Try it today:** if your business connects two groups, which group is harder to win, and could the other side pay so it joins first?

image.label: A single lit restaurant window on a dark city street
image.brief: 어두운 도시 거리에서 불이 켜진 식당 창문 하나. 안에 손님들의 따뜻한 실루엣. 1950년대 분위기.

factChecks.note: '지갑을 두고 온 저녁 식사'(이른바 First Supper, 1949년 뉴욕) 이야기는 널리 알려졌지만, 초기 홍보 담당이었던 Matty Simmons가 훗날 홍보용으로 꾸민 이야기라고 밝혔다고 전해집니다. 제안된 각도를 사실로 쓰지 않고 'a story often told'와 'reportedly'로 표시했습니다. Simmons의 회고록과 당시 보도로 확인하세요.
Frank McNamara와 Ralph Schneider의 공동 창업, 1950년 출범은 Diners Club 공식 연혁 기준입니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1950년 2월 McNamara·Schneider(Simmons·Bloomingdale 포함) 창업 확인.
가맹 식당 수수료 '약 7%'는 여러 결제 역사 자료에 나오는 수치입니다. 회사 연혁이나 당시 보도로 확인하세요. 회원 연회비 금액은 자료마다 달라 'a small yearly fee'로만 적었습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 가맹점 수수료 초기 7% 확인.
초기 가맹 식당 수(자료에 따라 14곳 또는 27곳)와 초기 회원 수(약 200명)는 자료마다 달라 'a small group of Manhattan restaurants', 'a few hundred'로 정성 표현했습니다.
Diners Club 이전의 백화점·석유회사 카드가 한 회사에서만 쓰이는 카드였다는 점, Diners Club이 여러 가맹점에서 쓰는 최초의 범용 charge card로 널리 기록된다는 점을 확인하세요.
American Express와 BankAmericard의 카드 출시(1958년)는 각 회사 연혁으로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] American Express·BankAmericard 1958년은 이번 검색에서 미확인.

sources.text: Simmons, M. (1995). The Credit Card Catastrophe: The 20th Century Phenomenon That Changed the World. Barricade Books.
Mandell, L. (1990). The Credit Card Industry: A History. Twayne Publishers.
